notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (tjmaxx.tjx.com, 200) checked first - no anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web directive anywhere; only blanket User-agent:* rules, so no Claude-specific disallow to respect. TREE: full category tree from https://tjmaxx.tjx.com/store/sitewide/json/navMenuData.jsp via curl_cffi impersonate=safari17_2_ios (HTTP 200, 667,005 bytes, 3,124 nodes, navigationHierarchy with itemCount per node) - the same route the prior Home-Decor pass used. The mobile host endpoints named in the task brief are Marshalls-shaped and do NOT exist on TJ Maxx: https://m.tjmaxx.tjx.com/us/m/sitewide/json/navMenuData.jsp -> 404, and https://m.tjmaxx.tjx.com/us/m/swipe/list/_/N-<n> -> 404 on all three profiles tried; TJ Maxx mobile paths are /m/... with no /us/ segment. https://m.tjmaxx.tjx.com/m/sitemap.jsp and https://tjmaxx.tjx.com/store/sitemap.jsp both returned 200 (878 KB) and were used as an independent cross-check of the department list; they corroborate that Furniture & Lighting is the only furniture-bearing department. FURNITURE LOCATED: I regex-scanned all 3,124 nodes for furnit|sofa|couch|sectional|loveseat|chair|seating|table|desk|bed|headboard|dresser|nightstand|wardrobe|armoire|cabinet|bookcase|shelv|stool|bench|ottoman|pouf|recliner|daybed|chest|vanity|console|tv stand|crib|nursery|patio|sideboard|credenza|futon|barstool. Outside the duplicated 'new arrivals', 'the runway' and 'clearance' facet-mirrors of the same tree, the ONLY furniture nodes in the entire catalogue are Home > Shop by Category > Furniture & Lighting (itemCount 624) with exactly three children: chairs & seating (197), lighting (219), tables (183). Both furniture children have childCategories=[] in the feed and their on-page category rail shows no deeper level, so they are true leaves (the feed is not depth-capped - other branches go four levels deep, e.g. home > shop by category > bed & bath > bath > bath accessories). Kids & Baby contains no nursery/crib/kids-furniture node anywhere. QTY: the rendered listing header was obtained for one leaf. A curl_cffi profile sweep found impersonate=safari18_0_ios opened https://tjmaxx.tjx.com/store/shop/home-shop-by-category-furniture-lighting-chairs-seating/_/N-2995848529 once (HTTP 200, 1,289,972 bytes of genuine listing HTML): title 'High Quality Affordable Chairs & Seating | TJ Maxx', h1 'chairs & seating', header text 'chairs & seating 197 items' - EXACTLY equal to that node's navMenuData itemCount of 197. That is a same-session, same-node confirmation that itemCount is the rendered total on this site, on top of the prior pass's three-way validation (Decorative Accessories 809 header = ceil(809/180)=5 pages = itemCount 809). TABLES HEADER UNOBTAINABLE: after that single success TJX IP-blocked all listing HTML - the tables URL was retried 16 times across ~25 minutes on safari18_0_ios/safari17_2_ios/safari17_0/safari18_0/chrome124/chrome116, on both the desktop /store/shop/ and mobile /m/shop/ paths, and every response was the 41 KB /securityfailover 'Something went wrong.' deny shell; a replay of the chairs URL that had just succeeded also returned the deny shell, confirming an IP-level throttle rather than a per-URL rule. r.jina.ai returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' 403 on both leaves and on two retries (shared-proxy contention), WebFetch returned HTTP 403, m-tjmaxx-tjx-com.translate.goog returned 403, and a Googlebot UA returned 403. The navMenuData JSON endpoint itself stayed reachable throughout. Tables therefore rests on itemCount, which brief section 4 lists as known-exact-under-check for TJX Endeca and which I validated against the rendered header on its sibling node in this same session; evidence says so explicitly. SANITY CHECKS: navMenuData was fetched twice; itemCount was byte-identical on the second read for chairs & seating (197), tables (183), furniture & lighting (624), lighting (219) and outdoor (175), so no intra-session drift. The counts differ per node rather than repeating one site-wide figure, and none is a suspiciously round number. Scope of chairs & seating was verified from the 180 product titles on the page I did open - every one is furniture (e.g. '30x20 Gina Swivel Anywhere Chair', '61.25x26 Revival Tufted Bench', '19in Darcy Ruffle Skirt Storage Ottoman', '41x30 Eli Power Recliner Chair', 'Set Of 2 20x40 Meliz Swivel Counter Stools', '55x29x25 Low Back Loveseat With Storage', '2pc Burl Wood Table And Bench Set'), with zero cushions, seat pads or non-furniture strays; 180 titles is the page-1 cap of 180, consistent with a 197 total. EXCLUDED: Lighting (219) under the same department - lighting is out of scope. Outdoor (itemCount 175) is excluded: it has childCategories=[] in today's feed, so the seasonal split the prior August pass saw (Outdoor Furniture 15, Outdoor Decor 60, Outdoor Rugs, Outdoor Pillows & Cushions, Outdoor Entertaining, Beach & Pool) has collapsed into one undifferentiated mixed roll-up whose primary product types are decor, rugs, textiles and entertaining as much as furniture; there is no furniture-only outdoor node left to take and its 175 total cannot be attributed to furniture. Back to Campus > Furniture & Lighting (84) excluded as a seasonal promotional collection and a re-cut of the same items. Shop by Room (Bathroom 262 / Bedroom 826 / Kitchen & Dining Room 705 / Living Room 671) and Shop by Style (Global Home / Home Essentials / Neutral Living) excluded - all have childCategories=[] and are room/style re-cuts of the ENTIRE Home department mixing bedding, textiles, kitchen and decor with furniture, not furniture-typed nodes; a room name alone never decides. Home > New Arrivals, Home > Clearance, Fall Decor, Halloween and every 'view all' node dropped as section 3 navigation junk. Also excluded as non-furniture: Bed & Bath, Kitchen & Tabletop (incl. Table & Kitchen Linens - linens, not tables), Pillows & Decor and all its children, Luggage & Travel, Pet, Stationery. FOOTNOTE: 197 + 219 + 183 = 599 against the parent's 624, so ~25 items sit in Furniture & Lighting without a child assignment; I did not attribute them anywhere, and no parent total was used as or summed into a child total.
